chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār narrated from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from Aḥmad ibn ʿUmar, who said:

I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who performed wudu (ablution) and forgot to wipe his head until he had stood in salat (prayer). He said: “Whoever forgets wiping his head, or anything from the wudu (ablution) that Allah, Exalted is He, mentioned in the Qur’an, must repeat the salat (prayer).”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah, Exalted is He, support him, said: It suffices a person in wiping his head that he wipe the front part of it by the measure of one finger, placing it across it along with the hair to its hairline. If he wipes from it the measure of three joined fingers in width, then he has performed it fully and done what is more excellent. Likewise, it suffices him in wiping his feet that he wipe each one of them with the tip of his index finger from their toes to the ankles; but if he wipes them with his two palms, that is more excellent.
What indicates that is His saying, Exalted is He: “And wipe your heads and your feet up to the ankles.”

Whoever wipes his head and his feet with one finger has fallen under the designation and is called one who wipes. What is less than a finger is not binding in that regard, because if we were left with the apparent wording, we would have said that such a thing is permissible, but the sunnah (prophetic tradition) has prevented it; and that also indicates the permissibility of that.

key_terms.السُّنَّةَ: the sunnah (prophetic tradition), which restricts what the apparent wording alone might suggest
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: salat (prayer), which must be repeated if the required wiping was omitted
key_terms.الْكَعْبَيْنِ: the ankles, the endpoint for wiping the feet
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification before salat (prayer)
key_terms.رَأْسِهِ: his head, the part to be wiped in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.مَسْحَ: wiping with moisture as required in wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: What happens if someone forgets to wipe the head in wudu (ablution) before salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This report states that if a person omits wiping the head, or another Qur’anically mandated part of wudu (ablution), and then enters salat (prayer), he must repeat the salat (prayer). It also explains the minimum sufficient and preferred extent of wiping the head and feet, grounding the ruling in the Qur’anic command to wipe the head and feet.
